To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

three fully automated serological SARS CoV-2 antibody assays, Abbott, DiaSorin and Roche, have a very high specificity of 99%, but a low sensitivity of 80 90%, which is in contrast to the manufacturers’ specifications.
we compared three SARS CoV-2 antibody assays and found that the sensitivities and the specificities are similar.
we found differences in specificities between the three SARS CoV antibody assays by Abbott Roche and Dia Sorin that have a relevant impact on the positive predictive value.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the question of whether the three fully automated Sars CoV 2 anti body tests by Abbott, Rothe and DiaSorine can be used in the diagnosis of Covid 19 and whether the test results can be compared with each other.
the question of how to best assess the performance of SARS Cov 2 antibody assays in the future.
the development and evaluation of a novel rapid and sensitive test system for the detection of antibodies against SARS-CoV-2 in serum.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Abbott assay is the least sensitive and the least specific assay, the Roche assay is the most sensitive and the most specific assay and the DiaSorin assay is a good compromise in between. However
all three methods are suitable for the screening of SARS Co V2 antibody seroprevalencies, but not for the diagnosis of SARS Co2 infections.
all three assays can be used for screening, but that they are not suitable for the confirmation of positive screening results.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Roche test has the highest specificity and sensitivity, while Abbott and DiaSorina have the highest sensitivity and specificity, respectively.
the three SARS CoV assays have high specificities, but low sensitivities, and that the results of the DiaSorin assay are not in line with the results of the Abbott and Roche assays.
the Abbott assay is the best choice for screening of a low risk population, the DiaSorin assay is the best option for screening of a high risk population, and Roche is a good compromise for both.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is not possible to directly compare the positive predictive values of these tests at different levels of disease prevalence.
it is crucial to carefully evaluate new tests before implementing them into routine diagnostics, especially in the current situation where many new tests are introduced into clinical practice.
it is not enough to simply report the sensitivity and specificity of serological assays.
